event_cain_murders_abel.title: Cain builds a city
event_cain_murders_abel.note: The draft: fall → exile → human striving (4:8; 4:11–16; 4:17). The text gives a judgment (4:11–12) and a mercy, the mark (4:15); the city (4:17) is held, no family stage.

event_cain_murders_abel.title: Abel over Cain
event_cain_murders_abel.note: Cain born first (4:1–2); "the LORD looked with favor on Abel" (4:4); Cain "very angry" (4:5). A reading: the text does not frame it as elder and younger.

event_hagar_ishmael_in_the_wilderness.title: Hagar & Ishmael
event_hagar_ishmael_in_the_wilderness.note: The draft: judgment → mercy → restoration. The text is an expulsion, not a judgment on Hagar; she weeps and God hears the boy (21:16–17), then opens her eyes to a well.

event_hagar_ishmael_in_the_wilderness.title: Isaac over Ishmael
event_hagar_ishmael_in_the_wilderness.note: "Through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned" (21:12). Ishmael the elder is implied by the story, not stated in these verses.

event_jacobs_household_purges_idols.title: Jacob purges idols
event_jacobs_household_purges_idols.note: The draft: exile → return → covenant renewal (Gen 34 as background). Relabelled: Shechem's aftermath, the return to Bethel, the name Israel and the charge to be fruitful.

arc_joseph_in_egypt.title: Joseph interprets dreams
arc_joseph_in_egypt.note: The arc runs past the one event: prison (39), the dreams (40), Pharaoh (41).

event_moses_flees_to_midian.title: Moses flees to Midian
event_moses_flees_to_midian.note: Stages trimmed so they do not overlap (the draft: 2:11–15, 2:15–22, 2:21–22). The flight to Midian is now part of the descent; the raising is the call from the bush, "I am sending you to Pharaoh" (3:10) -- a reading.

event_moses_flees_to_midian.title: Moses at the well of Midian
event_moses_flees_to_midian.shown: Moses at the well of Midian
event_moses_flees_to_midian.family_name: Meeting at a well, then marriage

arc_the_call_of_moses.title: Burning bush
arc_the_call_of_moses.note: The draft: anointing → empowerment → mission. Moses objects five times (3:11, 3:13, 4:1, 4:10, 4:13); the name and the signs answer him. The mission (4:18–23) is past the event, so the arc is the instance.

arc_the_red_sea.title: Red Sea
arc_the_red_sea.note: The draft: bondage → deliverance → covenant. The Israelites cry out (14:10); the Egyptians are drowned (14:26–31); the draft's covenant stage is the Song (15:1–21), praise. The Song is past the event: the arc is the instance.

arc_the_golden_calf.title: Golden calf
arc_the_golden_calf.note: Moses intercedes twice (32:11–14, 32:30–32) inside the draft's judgment stage; the judgment is split around them. Mercy and restoration are Exod 33–34: the arc.

arc_the_tabernacle.title: Tabernacle
arc_the_tabernacle.note: The draft's line names chaos, but its stages begin at the word; no chaos stage.

event_twelve_spies_sent_.title: Twelve spies
event_twelve_spies_sent_.note: Moses' intercession and the pardon (14:13–20) sit between failure and judgment: this event also has the judgment-and-mercy shape inside it.

event_bronze_serpent.title: Bronze serpent
event_bronze_serpent.note: The draft: judgment 21:4–6, mercy 21:7–8. The people speak against God (21:5), then confess and Moses prays (21:7): the turning.

event_crossing_the_jordan.title: Jordan crossing
event_crossing_the_jordan.note: The text's order is word, then the waters stand; the memorial stones (presence) are cut out of the draft's order stage.

event_fall_of_jericho.title: Rahab spared
event_fall_of_jericho.note: "Only Rahab the prostitute and all those with her in her house will live" (6:17); "she has lived among the Israelites to this day" (6:25). No corruption stage: the chapter names none for Jericho.

arc_achan_and_ai.title: Achan
arc_achan_and_ai.note: Joshua falls before the ark and prays (7:6–9). No mercy stage; the restoration (Ai) is past the event: the arc.

arc_the_call_of_gideon.title: Gideon’s fleece
arc_the_call_of_gideon.note: The draft: testing → reassurance → commissioning. Gideon objects (6:15) and asks for signs twice (6:17, 6:36–37): the call shape, across the chapter.

arc_gideon_against_midian.title: Gideon’s 300
arc_gideon_against_midian.note: The draft's 'order' stage (the reduction, 7:1–8) is the call's mission above; held here.

event_judges_raised_up.title: Samson & Delilah
event_judges_raised_up.note: The draft: fall → death → resurrection (symbolic). The symbolic stage is not declared by the text and is dropped; Samson calls on the LORD (16:28) and is strengthened.

event_judges_raised_up.title: Othniel
event_judges_raised_up.note: The cycle the text states (Judg 2:11–19), first told of Othniel: 'the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and He raised up Othniel' (3:9); 'the land had rest forty years' (3:11).

event_ruths_redemption.title: Boaz redeems Ruth
event_ruths_redemption.note: The draft: restoration → covenant → mission. The elders' blessing (4:11–12) and 'the LORD enabled her to conceive' (4:13) read as promise and fulfilment.

event_solomons_wisdom.title: Solomon’s judgment
event_solomons_wisdom.note: The draft: chaos → wisdom → order. The king's word (3:24–25) makes the order; the wisdom is named at 3:28.

event_elishas_miracles.title: Naaman
event_elishas_miracles.note: Trimmed so the stages do not overlap (the draft: 5:1–14, 5:13–14, 5:14–19).

event_elishas_miracles.title: Shunammite’s son
event_elishas_miracles.note: Elisha shuts the door and prays to the LORD (4:33) before the boy lives.

arc_the_return_under_ezra.title: Ezra’s return
arc_the_return_under_ezra.note: The draft: exile → return → covenant renewal. The descent is the exile Ezra names: "carried away to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar" (2:1); the return and Ezra's coming, the raising. Ezra 9–10 (the confession) is a turning, not part of this shape.

event_wall_rebuilt.title: Nehemiah’s walls
event_wall_rebuilt.note: The draft: chaos → order → restoration. 'Let us rebuild' (2:17–18) is the word; the enemies see 'this work had been done by our God' (6:16).

arc_esther_and_purim.title: Esther intervenes
arc_esther_and_purim.note: The draft's two templates (Esther intervenes; Purim) are one deliverance: the decree, Mordecai's loud cry (4:1), Haman hanged, the enemies struck, the feast.

arc_esther_and_purim.title: Haman’s plot
arc_esther_and_purim.family_name: Meant for evil, turned to good
arc_esther_and_purim.note: Hanged on the gallows he built (7:10); "their plan was overturned" (9:1); "their sorrow turned to joy" (9:22).

arc_job.title: Job restored
arc_job.note: The draft: descent → ascent → restoration. God's speeches (38–41) end in Job's repentance (42:1–6): the humbling.

arc_job.title: Job tested
arc_job.note: "In all this, Job did not sin" (1:22). The same arc is Brought low, raised up.

event_daniel_interprets_dreams.title: Nebuchadnezzar’s madness
event_daniel_interprets_dreams.note: The draft: descent → judgment → restoration. The pride (4:30), the sentence, 'I lifted my eyes to heaven' (4:34).

arc_jonah.title: Jonah swallowed
arc_jonah.note: Symbolic, and kept because the text declares it: 'as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish' (Matt 12:40).

event_nineveh_repents.title: Nineveh repents
event_nineveh_repents.note: The draft's 'mercy' (3:5–9) is the repentance — the turning; the mercy is God relenting (3:10).

event_birth_of_john_the_baptist.title: Birth of John
event_birth_of_john_the_baptist.note: Zechariah's doubt and silence (1:18–22) is the obstacle.

event_birth_of_john_the_baptist.title: Elizabeth’s son
event_birth_of_john_the_baptist.note: "Elizabeth was barren" (1:7); "your prayer has been heard" (1:13).

event_ananias_sapphira.title: Ananias & Sapphira
event_ananias_sapphira.note: Judgment without mercy. the draft's 'purification' (5:11, the fear) is held.

event_david_defeats_goliath.title: David and Goliath
event_david_defeats_goliath.note: From the Enemy list: 'the LORD saves … the battle is the LORD's' (17:47).

event_hezekiahs_deliverance.title: Sennacherib against Jerusalem
event_hezekiahs_deliverance.note: From the Enemy list. Hezekiah's prayer is the cry: 'please save us from his hand' (19:19).

event_gerasene_demoniac.title: Legion
event_gerasene_demoniac.note: From the Enemy list: a bondage no one could subdue (5:4) as the threat; 'tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy He has shown you' (5:19) as the praise.

arc_paul_and_silas_at_philippi.title: Paul and Silas freed
arc_paul_and_silas_at_philippi.note: From the Enemy list. Praying and singing at midnight (16:25) as the cry; they do not leave when the doors open, and the rescue the text dwells on is the jailer's: 'what must I do to be saved?' (16:30).

event_peter_freed_by_angel.title: Peter freed
event_peter_freed_by_angel.note: The church prays earnestly (12:5): the cry.

arc_the_fall_of_babylon.title: Fall of Babylon
arc_the_fall_of_babylon.note: The draft: judgment → fall → restoration. Its 'fall' is Babylon falling (the judgment); her sin is 17:1–6. No mercy.

arc_the_flood.title: The flood
arc_the_flood.note: "Only Noah and those with him in the ark remained" (7:23); the LORD shut him in (7:16). One of the two stories Jesus draws the pattern from (Luke 17:26–27).

event_destruction_of_sodom.title: Sodom
event_destruction_of_sodom.note: "Get up! ... or you will be swept away in the punishment of the city" (19:15); "He brought Lot out of the catastrophe" (19:29). The other story Jesus draws it from (Luke 17:28–29).

event_korahs_rebellion.title: Korah
event_korahs_rebellion.note: "Move away now from the tents of these wicked men ... or you will be swept away" (16:26), the words said to Lot (Gen 19:15). The remnant is the congregation spared: Aaron "stood between the living and the dead" (16:48).

event_elijah_at_horeb.title: Elijah’s seven thousand
event_elijah_at_horeb.note: "I have reserved seven thousand in Israel — all whose knees have not bowed to Baal" (19:18); the charge passes to Elisha (19:19–21).

arc_the_mark_on_the_foreheads.title: The mark on the foreheads
arc_the_mark_on_the_foreheads.note: A vision, whose city the text names (9:4, 9:9): "do not go near anyone who has the mark" (9:6); Ezekiel asks, "will You destroy the entire remnant of Israel?" (9:8).

arc_the_passover.title: The Passover
arc_the_passover.note: The blood distinguishes the houses (12:13) and the LORD "spared our homes" (12:27). A reading: the text does not call Israel a remnant here, and the same night is the Red Sea story's beginning.

arc_jerusalem_falls_a_remnant_left.arc: Jerusalem falls, a remnant left (2 Kgs 24–25; Ezra 1–9)
arc_jerusalem_falls_a_remnant_left.title: Jerusalem’s remnant
arc_jerusalem_falls_a_remnant_left.shown: Jerusalem falls, a remnant left (2 Kgs 24–25; Ezra 1–9)
arc_jerusalem_falls_a_remnant_left.note: "The captain of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land" (25:12); the returned community calls itself the remnant: "we remain this day as a remnant" (Ezra 9:15).

event_binding_of_isaac.title: Abraham tested
event_binding_of_isaac.note: "God tested Abraham" (22:1); "now I know that you fear God" (22:12); "because you have done this ... I will surely bless you" (22:16–17).

arc_daniels_test.title: Daniel’s test
arc_daniels_test.note: "Please test your servants for ten days" (1:12); "they entered the king's service" (1:19).

event_jesus_temptation.title: Jesus tempted
event_jesus_temptation.note: "Led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted" (4:1); "angels came and ministered to Him" (4:11) read as what follows faithfulness.

arc_hezekiah_shows_his_treasures.arc: Hezekiah shows his treasures (2 Kgs 20; 2 Chr 32)
arc_hezekiah_shows_his_treasures.title: Hezekiah’s treasures
arc_hezekiah_shows_his_treasures.shown: Hezekiah shows his treasures (2 Kgs 20; 2 Chr 32)
arc_hezekiah_shows_his_treasures.note: "God left him alone to test him, that He might know all that was in Hezekiah's heart" (2 Chr 32:31); the envoys are shown everything (2 Kgs 20:13); "nothing will be left" (20:17).

arc_joseph_and_his_brothers.title: Joseph’s brothers
arc_joseph_and_his_brothers.family_name: Meant for evil, turned to good
arc_joseph_and_his_brothers.note: The text's own statement of the pattern: "what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good ... to preserve the lives of many people" (50:20).

arc_balaam_hired_to_curse.title: Balaam hired to curse
arc_balaam_hired_to_curse.family_name: Meant for evil, turned to good
arc_balaam_hired_to_curse.note: "I summoned you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have persisted in blessing them" (Num 24:10); "the LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you" (Deut 23:5).

arc_joseph_makes_himself_known.title: Joseph makes himself known
arc_joseph_makes_himself_known.note: "They did not recognize him" (42:8); "I am Joseph" (45:3).

arc_esthers_hidden_people.title: Esther’s people
arc_esthers_hidden_people.note: "Esther did not reveal her people" (2:10); "my people and I have been sold out to destruction" (7:4).

event_road_to_emmaus.title: Road to Emmaus
event_road_to_emmaus.note: "Their eyes were kept from recognizing Him" (24:16); "their eyes were opened and they recognized Jesus" (24:31).

arc_mary_magdalene_at_the_tomb.title: Mary at the tomb
arc_mary_magdalene_at_the_tomb.note: "She did not recognize that it was Jesus" (20:14); "Mary." ... "Rabboni!" (20:16).

arc_the_call_of_jeremiah.title: The call of Jeremiah
arc_the_call_of_jeremiah.note: "I surely do not know how to speak, for I am only a child!" (1:6); the LORD touches his mouth (1:9).

arc_the_call_of_isaiah.title: The call of Isaiah
arc_the_call_of_isaiah.note: "Woe is me ... a man of unclean lips" (6:5) is unworthiness, not a refusal; the coal (6:6–7) answers it. The text's order: objection and sign before the call (6:8).

arc_isaac_promised_and_born.title: Isaac promised
arc_isaac_promised_and_born.note: "The LORD did for Sarah what He had promised" (21:1); she had laughed, being past age (18:11–12).

arc_samson_promised_and_born.title: Samson promised
arc_samson_promised_and_born.note: "Barren and had no children" (13:2); "you will conceive and give birth to a son" (13:3); "the woman gave birth to a son and named him Samson" (13:24).

arc_samson_promised_and_born.title: Manoah’s wife
arc_samson_promised_and_born.note: "His wife was barren and had no children" (13:2).

arc_amos_intercedes.title: Amos intercedes
arc_amos_intercedes.note: Twice: "Lord GOD, please forgive!" (7:2) ... "So the LORD relented" (7:3, 7:6).

arc_the_cross_and_the_resurrection.title: The cross and the resurrection
arc_the_cross_and_the_resurrection.note: It rests on the text's own explanation. Corruption: "sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned" (Rom 5:12) -- Genesis 3 and all who came after, in one verse; "There is no one righteous, not even one" (3:10) quotes Psalm 14, whose "corrupt" in 14:1 is the flood's verb, with God looking to see it as in Gen 6:12; "all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" (3:23). Judgment: "the day of wrath, when God's righteous judgment will be revealed" (Rom 2:5), and on the cross, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" (Matt 27:46). Set apart: "I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am" (John 17:24). Remnant: "everyone who believes in Him shall not perish" (John 3:16), sent to "make disciples of all nations" (Matt 28:19). New beginning: "He has risen" (Matt 28:6), and "if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!" (2 Cor 5:17). The text itself ties this story to the flood's: Peter sets the eight saved in the ark beside "the resurrection of Jesus Christ" (1 Pet 3:20–21), and Jesus takes "I will strike the Shepherd" to himself (Matt 26:31), where Zechariah goes on, "a third will be left" (Zech 13:7–8).

arc_sarahs_son.title: Sarah’s son
arc_sarahs_son.note: "Sarai was barren; she had no children" (11:30).

event_birth_of_jacob_and_esau.title: Rebekah’s twins
event_birth_of_jacob_and_esau.note: "Isaac prayed to the LORD on behalf of his wife, because she was barren" (25:21).

event_birth_of_jacob_and_esau.title: Jacob over Esau
event_birth_of_jacob_and_esau.note: "The older will serve the younger" (25:23); "may the sons of your mother bow down to you" (27:29); Esau's "loud and bitter cry" (27:34).

arc_rachels_son.title: Rachel’s son
arc_rachels_son.note: "Rachel was barren" (29:31); "God remembered Rachel. He listened to her" (30:22) read as a prayer the text does not quote.

event_birth_and_calling_of_samuel.title: Hannah
event_birth_and_calling_of_samuel.note: Barrenness and a rival's taunting as the threat; "the LORD remembered her" (1:19); "I rejoice in Your salvation" (2:1).

arc_jacob_over_esau.title: Jacob over Esau
arc_jacob_over_esau.note: "The older will serve the younger" (25:23); "may the sons of your mother bow down to you" (27:29); Esau's "loud and bitter cry" (27:34).

event_jacob_blesses_ephraim_manasseh.title: Ephraim over Manasseh
event_jacob_blesses_ephraim_manasseh.note: "Although Manasseh was the firstborn" (48:14); "his younger brother shall be greater than he" (48:19).

event_david_anointed.title: David among his brothers
event_david_anointed.note: "There is still the youngest ... he is tending the sheep" (16:11).

event_josephs_dreams.title: Joseph over his brothers
event_josephs_dreams.note: "Born to him in his old age" (37:3); the sheaves bow (37:7); "Do you intend to reign over us?" (37:8).

arc_a_wife_for_isaac.title: A wife for Isaac
arc_a_wife_for_isaac.family_name: Meeting at a well, then marriage

arc_jacob_meets_rachel.title: Jacob meets Rachel
arc_jacob_meets_rachel.family_name: Meeting at a well, then marriage

arc_the_covenant_sealed_at_sinai.title: The covenant sealed at Sinai
arc_the_covenant_sealed_at_sinai.note: "All the words that the LORD has spoken, we will do" (24:3); "This is the blood of the covenant" (24:8). The first telling, not a renewal.

event_covenant_renewal_at_shechem.title: Covenant at Shechem
event_covenant_renewal_at_shechem.note: "We will serve the LORD our God" (24:24).

event_josiahs_reforms.title: Josiah’s covenant
event_josiahs_reforms.note: The king "made a covenant before the LORD" and "all the people entered into the covenant" (23:3): one verse, both stages.

event_asas_reforms_wars.title: Asa’s covenant
event_asas_reforms_wars.note: "They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD" (15:12); "They took an oath" (15:14).

arc_the_nations_left_to_test_israel.arc: The nations left to test Israel (Judg 2:20–3:8)
arc_the_nations_left_to_test_israel.title: The nations left to test Israel
arc_the_nations_left_to_test_israel.shown: The nations left to test Israel (Judg 2:20–3:8)
arc_the_nations_left_to_test_israel.note: "These nations were left to test the Israelites, to find out whether they would keep the commandments of the LORD" (3:4); they served the Baals (3:7) and were sold to Cushan-rishathaim (3:8).

event_manna_given.title: The manna test
event_manna_given.note: "In this way I will test whether or not they will follow My instructions" (16:4). The consequence is a rebuke, "How long will you refuse ...?" (16:28), and the spoiled manna (16:20).

event_water_from_the_rock_.title: Moses at Meribah
event_water_from_the_rock_.note: "Because you did not trust Me ... you will not bring this assembly into the land" (20:12). The text does not call the command a test: a reading.

event_sauls_disobedience_rejection.title: Saul spares Agag
event_sauls_disobedience_rejection.note: "Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has rejected you as king" (15:23). A command, not called a test: a reading.

arc_the_command_in_eden.title: The command in Eden
arc_the_command_in_eden.note: "You must not eat from the tree" (2:17); "because you ... have eaten from the tree of which I commanded you not to eat" (3:17). Not called a test: a reading.

arc_deborah_and_barak.title: Deborah and Barak
arc_deborah_and_barak.note: The stated cycle a third time: "the Israelites again did evil" (4:1), "cried out to the LORD" (4:3), and the Song (5:1).

arc_the_flight_to_egypt.title: The flight to Egypt
arc_the_flight_to_egypt.note: "Herod is going to search for the Child to destroy Him" (2:13). No cry.

arc_elijah_raises_the_widows_son.arc: Elijah raises the widow’s son (1 Kgs 17:17–24)
arc_elijah_raises_the_widows_son.title: Elijah raises the widow’s son
arc_elijah_raises_the_widows_son.shown: Elijah raises the widow’s son (1 Kgs 17:17–24)
arc_elijah_raises_the_widows_son.note: "O LORD my God, please let this boy's life return to him!" (17:21).

event_raising_of_lazarus.title: Lazarus
event_raising_of_lazarus.note: "Father, I thank You that You have heard Me" (11:41) before "Lazarus, come out!"

arc_jesus_dies_and_rises.title: Jesus dies and rises
arc_jesus_dies_and_rises.note: "He is not here; He has risen, just as He said" (28:6).

arc_ehud.title: Ehud
arc_ehud.note: The same stated cycle, second time: 'again they cried out to the LORD, and He raised up Ehud … as their deliverer' (3:15); 'Moab was subdued' (3:30). On the Enemy list too.

event_josephs_rise_in_egypt.title: Joseph interprets dreams
event_josephs_rise_in_egypt.note: The arc runs past the one event: prison (39), the dreams (40), Pharaoh (41).

event_joseph_interprets_dreams_in_prison.title: Joseph interprets dreams
event_joseph_interprets_dreams_in_prison.note: The arc runs past the one event: prison (39), the dreams (40), Pharaoh (41).

event_crucifixion.title: The cross and the resurrection
event_crucifixion.note: It rests on the text's own explanation. Corruption: "sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned" (Rom 5:12) -- Genesis 3 and all who came after, in one verse; "There is no one righteous, not even one" (3:10) quotes Psalm 14, whose "corrupt" in 14:1 is the flood's verb, with God looking to see it as in Gen 6:12; "all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" (3:23). Judgment: "the day of wrath, when God's righteous judgment will be revealed" (Rom 2:5), and on the cross, "My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?" (Matt 27:46). Set apart: "I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am" (John 17:24). Remnant: "everyone who believes in Him shall not perish" (John 3:16), sent to "make disciples of all nations" (Matt 28:19). New beginning: "He has risen" (Matt 28:6), and "if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!" (2 Cor 5:17). The text itself ties this story to the flood's: Peter sets the eight saved in the ark beside "the resurrection of Jesus Christ" (1 Pet 3:20–21), and Jesus takes "I will strike the Shepherd" to himself (Matt 26:31), where Zechariah goes on, "a third will be left" (Zech 13:7–8).
event_crucifixion.via_arc: Story arc: The cross and the resurrection (Matt 27–28)

event_ehud_assassinates_eglon.title: Ehud
event_ehud_assassinates_eglon.note: The same stated cycle, second time: 'again they cried out to the LORD, and He raised up Ehud … as their deliverer' (3:15); 'Moab was subdued' (3:30). On the Enemy list too.

judgment_mercy.name: Sin, judgment and mercy
judgment_mercy.note: A wrong, judgment on it, a turning (repentance or intercession), mercy, and restoration. Some instances end at judgment.

deliverance.name: Cry and rescue
deliverance.note: A threat or bondage, a cry, deliverance, the oppressor judged, praise. The text states it in Judges 2:11–19: they did evil, He gave them over, they groaned, He raised up judges who saved them.

descent_return.name: Brought low, raised up
descent_return.note: Going down — into prison, exile or loss — often a time of humbling, and being raised again, often to a task.

call.name: Called, reluctant, sent
call.note: God calls, the one called objects, a sign is given, and the mission begins.

promise.name: Promise kept
promise.note: A promise, what stands in its way (barrenness, doubt), and its fulfilment.

word_order.name: The word brings order
word_order.note: The word spoken, order made by it, and a presence or memorial at the end.

testing_failure.name: Tested and failed
testing_failure.note: A test failed and its consequence — the counter-shape of deliverance and call.

instances.title: Hezekiah shows his treasures (2 Kgs 20; 2 Chr 32)
The nations left to test Israel (Judg 2:20–3:8)

death_life.name: Death to life
death_life.note: Death, sometimes a prayer, and life given back.

instances.title: Elijah raises the widow’s son (1 Kgs 17:17–24)

remnant.name: Judgment and a remnant spared
remnant.note: Wickedness, those to be spared set apart (the ark, led out, the mark), a judgment that takes the rest, a remnant left, and sometimes a new beginning. Jesus draws it from Noah and Lot (Luke 17:26–30).

instances.title: Jerusalem falls, a remnant left (2 Kgs 24–25; Ezra 1–9)

tested_faithful.name: Tested and found faithful
tested_faithful.note: A test the text names as a test ("God tested Abraham", Gen 22:1), a faithful answer, and what follows it — the counter-shape of Tested and failed.

evil_to_good.name: Meant for evil, turned to good
evil_to_good.note: Harm planned, the plan turned back, and good from it. The text says it of itself: "what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good" (Gen 50:20); and Paul says it of all things, "God works all things together for the good of those who love Him" (Rom 8:28) -- read here as the same pattern, stated generally.

recognition.name: Hidden, then revealed
recognition.note: Someone not known for who they are ("they did not recognize him"), then made known ("I am Joseph").

barren.name: The barren woman conceives
barren.note: A woman the text calls barren, sometimes a prayer or a promise, and a son born: Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Manoah's wife, Hannah, Elizabeth.

younger.name: The younger over the elder
younger.note: The elder named, sometimes his protest, and the younger preferred. Stated at the start: "the older will serve the younger" (Gen 25:23).

well.name: Meeting at a well, then marriage
well.note: A journey to a far country, a well, water drawn, a girl running home to tell it, and a marriage: Rebekah, Rachel, Zipporah.

instances.title: Moses at the well of Midian

covenant_renewal.name: Covenant renewed before the people
covenant_renewal.note: The people gathered, the covenant read or set out, their answer ("we will serve the LORD"), and the covenant made or sealed.

held.Creation of Eve: a making and a union; none of the eight shapes
held.Melchizedek blesses Abraham: a blessing, not an anointing or a call
held.Balaam: God overrules a hired prophet to bless; none of the eight shapes
held.Temple tax coin: a question and a provision; none of the eight shapes
held.Fig tree: a judgment and a teaching on faith; none of the eight shapes
held.Seven churches: each letter is its own instance; to be built per letter
held.Paul stoned: resurrection (symbolic) is not declared by the text
held.Purim: joined with 'Esther intervenes' as one deliverance
